notes: 16 cases: 10 positive / 6 negative. All 10 positives are BYTE-VERBATIM production user turns extracted programmatically from ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl — not retyped, not tidied. They are the 10 distinct surface forms found among 98 resume-class turns across 4,002 transcripts, deduplicated case-insensitively and taken most-recent-first. The 6 negatives are AUTHORED single-axis near-misses: each one shares vocabulary with a positive but wants a different skill or a different object, so a trigger keyed on the bare word 'resume'/'continue' over-fires on them. REGISTER: production resume turns are terse and lowercase (65 of 98 are the bare word 'resume'); the negatives are written in the same register so polarity is not confounded with style. TRIGGER SURFACE: unlike handoff — where 30 of 31 production invocations named the skill literally — a resume turn NEVER names a skill; it is one to eight words of plain instruction. The whole routing load is therefore paraphrase inference, which is why the negative half matters more here than in a slash-command-shaped skill.

execution_status.statement: This case set has NOT been run through role-x.py eval. It is authored to the house format and its positives' provenance is verified (see verification_log), but no pass rate is claimed. Quoting a pass rate that no run produced is the failure this field exists to prevent. Run before promoting the skill past candidate.

verification_log.method: A regex over user-type records (isSidechain excluded by construction — 0 of 98 hits were sidechain) matching resume/continue/carry-on/pick-up openings on turns of <=120 chars, excluding system-reminder and local-command-caveat injections. 98 hits. Deduplicated case-insensitively on the trimmed text -> 10 distinct forms, all of which appear here as positives.
verification_log.distribution: 65 bare 'resume' · 19 'continue from where you left off' · 3 'resume please' · 2 'continue' · 2 'continue /autonomous' · 2 'carry on, continue /autonomous, resume the /loop' · 2 'carry on' · 1 'please resume' · 1 'continue please' · 1 'please continue, fix the problems and confirm its all clean and proper'
verification_log.preceding_state: 44 of 98 were immediately preceded by an explicit API error record; 7 by a user interrupt; 26 had an async subagent or workflow spawn in flight at the time of death.
verification_log.negatives_are_authored: All 6. No production turn was found that uses resume-vocabulary while wanting a different skill, so the negative half could not be drawn from traces. Stated rather than disguised: the negatives measure a hypothesis about over-triggering, not an observed failure.

cases.rationale: The dominant form — 65 of 98. One word, no context, maximum ambiguity. This is the case the skill exists for.

cases.prompt: Continue from where you left off.
cases.rationale: Second most common (19). Explicitly names continuation, not conclusion.
Names the driver explicitly — the operator is asking for the ENGINE to be restarted, not just the next step taken. Procedure step 5.
Bare 'continue' with no object. Contrast with neg-05, where 'continue' takes an object.
Politeness particle must not change routing.
As real-06, on the other stem.

cases.prompt: please continue, fix the problems and confirm its all clean and proper
cases.rationale: Longest production form. Carries follow-on work, so a router that treats extra clauses as disqualifying will miss it. Typo 'its' preserved.
Names ANOTHER skill as the object of continuation. resume restores the arc; /autonomous is what it restores. Must not route to /autonomous alone, which would restart rather than resume.

cases.prompt: write a handoff so i can pick this up tomorrow
cases.rationale: Shares 'pick this up' with resume vocabulary, but asks for a DOC for a future context. That is handoff. Single axis: voluntary stop, artifact requested.

cases.prompt: whats blocking you, what do you need from me
cases.rationale: The arc has stopped, but on a human decision, not an external fault. That is handback.

cases.prompt: start a persist loop for this refactor
cases.rationale: Deliberate cross-context restarting. persist restarts contexts BY DESIGN; resume repairs one that was killed.

cases.prompt: resume the paused deployment on railway
cases.rationale: The sharpest negative. Contains the literal trigger word 'resume', but its object is an EXTERNAL system, not the agent's own arc. A keyword trigger fires here; a correct router does not.

cases.prompt: continue the sentence in that draft
cases.rationale: 'continue' with a content object. Contrast real-05, where bare 'continue' has no object and can only mean the arc.

cases.prompt: summarize where we landed on the auth work
cases.rationale: Asks for exactly the wrap-up that resume must NOT produce. If the skill fires here it has inverted its own contract.
